name: Capacities
subcategory: notes, wikis and personal knowledge bases
tagline: Organize linked notes as typed objects such as people, books, meetings, and ideas

tiers.name: Capacities Basic
tiers.limits: Unlimited spaces, objects, blocks, custom object types and devices; 5 GB media total, then 100 MB uploads/month; 100 MB/file

tiers.name: Capacities Pro
tiers.limits: Unlimited media uploads under fair use; 100 MB/file; AI, smart queries, calendar, tasks, formulas and API
tiers.notes: Free in-app trial; yearly billing is 16% lower.

tiers.name: Capacities Believer
tiers.limits: All Pro limits/features plus beta access to major new features
tiers.notes: Supporter plan; yearly billing is 16% lower.

pricing.freeTierCaps: Unlimited spaces, objects, blocks, custom object types and devices; 5 GB total media, then 100 MB uploads/month; 100 MB/file
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (-16%); free Pro trial in app, no card
pricing.hiddenCosts: Paid 'unlimited' media is subject to fair use and a 100 MB/file cap. Paddle applies regional pricing/VAT, and VPN-based regional pricing is not accepted. No team or organization plan is sold.

verdictSummary: The core loop is small enough for a capable coding agent to produce a useful local version in one sitting. For Capacities, organize linked notes as typed objects such as people, books, meetings, and ideas. The hard boundary is object-model polish, mobile capture, sync, calendar integration, and ai features, plus sync, collaboration, and capture polish.
coreLoopDIY: Capture linked notes as typed objects such as people, books, meetings, and ideas, search them instantly, surface backlinks, and export a normal Markdown folder.
requirements: optional sync folder chosen by the user
whatYouLose: object-model polish, mobile capture, sync, calendar integration, and AI features
ongoingBurden: file watching, conflict handling, indexing, mobile apps, encryption, backups, and migrations
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Capacities because people keep paying when the note system is trusted across every device and disappears into their daily capture habits. The recurring cost buys file watching, conflict handling, indexing, mobile apps, encryption, backups, and migrations, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: AppFlowy
priorArt.desc: Active open-source workspace with local-first documents and databases.

alternatives.name: Anytype
alternatives.desc: Capacities with the same object obsession, local data and only 100 MB of free relay storage.

facts.install: Official desktop or mobile installer; optional self-hosted Any-Sync network for advanced deployments
facts.dataFormat: Objects are encrypted and stored locally in Anytype's object store; optional encrypted peer/backup-node copies use Any-Sync, and exports are available as Markdown or Any-Block JSON
facts.gapVsPaid: Anytype's typed-object graph is rougher to navigate and gives up Capacities' polished calendar integrations, object workflows, and built-in AI experience.
facts.setupBlocker: The recovery Key must be saved because Anytype cannot recover it; local-only users must manage backups, while synced use is subject to the included network-storage allowance

alternatives.name: SiYuan
alternatives.desc: Typed blocks, relations and database views for people who enjoy seeing the machinery.

facts.install: Desktop/mobile package, or Docker image for browser-based self-hosting
facts.engines: Built-in AI features connect to OpenAI-compatible APIs using a configured endpoint and key
facts.dataFormat: A workspace stores block documents as structured .sy JSON files plus assets on disk; SQLite files hold indexes and auxiliary state; documents can export to Markdown, HTML, PDF, and Word
facts.gapVsPaid: SiYuan exposes blocks, attributes, and database mechanics more directly, so creating and browsing coherent object types is less elegant than in Capacities.
facts.setupBlocker: The desktop app installs cleanly, but free cross-device sync is not a turnkey feature: official cloud sync is a paid membership feature and Docker hosting does not transparently become desktop/mobile sync

alternatives.name: Trilium Notes
alternatives.desc: Notes become objects through attributes, relations and reusable templates.

facts.install: Desktop release package, or Docker Compose/image for a server and browser client
facts.dataFormat: Notes, hierarchy, attributes, revisions, and most attachments live in a local or server-side SQLite database named document.db; notes can be exported to HTML, Markdown, or OPML
facts.gapVsPaid: Trilium remains fundamentally tree-first, making typed objects and cross-cutting collections feel bolted on compared with Capacities' object-native design.
facts.setupBlocker: The desktop app is straightforward, but cross-device sync and browser access require operating a Trilium server, persisting document.db, and handling backups and upgrades

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Pro plan and a personal local knowledge base DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Capacities in an empty repository.
Use Tauri 2, React, TypeScript, SQLite, and Markdown files as the source of truth; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: capture linked notes as typed objects such as people, books, meetings, and ideas, search them instantly, surface backlinks, and export a normal Markdown folder.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Store one Markdown file per note and a small SQLite index that can be rebuilt at any time.
Support wiki links, tags, backlinks, daily notes, pinned notes, and full-text search.
Add a fast command palette and keyboard-first create, rename, move, and link actions.
Render Markdown with task lists, code blocks, tables, and local image attachments.
Detect external file changes and show a safe conflict-resolution view.
Provide full-folder export, import, and an index-rebuild command.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out proprietary sync servers.
Deliberately leave out real-time multiplayer documents.
Deliberately leave out a plugin marketplace and hosted public sites.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
